description:
Make our gripper attach to the Seeed reBot Arm B601-RS (gripper motor: RobStride RS00; see AGENTS.md hardware section and the Gripper N / Handle N / Base N scheme). Design the mounting interface so the latest gripper base (Base 9, voice-d96cd30d, built on Base 8; if a newer Base exists when you claim this, build on the latest) bolts onto the arm's wrist / end-effector flange in place of the stock reBot gripper. Use Seeed's reBot-DevArm repo (https://github.com/Seeed-Projects/reBot-DevArm) for the B601_RS hardware CAD and the stock gripper's mount, and match its bolt pattern and how the stock gripper mounts. Deliver a parameterized adapter (or an integrated mount on the base, whichever is cleaner) that prints without supports, with the RS00 cabling (CAN and power) routed cleanly. Don't break existing Base versions; this becomes the next Base N per the scheme. 

SCOPE EXPANSION (Jake, 2026-10-20):
Step 1 — Arm CAD: see whether CAD exists for the reBot Arm (bought from Seeed Studio), e.g. STEP or STL files in Seeed-Projects/reBot-DevArm under hardware/reBot_B601_RS. Bring it into the repo with its source URL and license noted, converted to something the live preview and OpenSCAD can use, so the arm shows in the live preview.
Step 2 — Dual end-effector mount: design a mount base on the arm's end flange that takes BOTH pieces of hardware Jake will have: (a) our two-finger gripper (latest Base) and (b) the Aero Hand (the left-handed Aero Hand already in use; find its CAD and mounting in this repo or the aero_hand project). Ideally one common arm-side flange adapter with swappable tool-side interfaces, or a quick-change, so either end effector can be mounted. Keep everything parameterized and printable without supports.

results.identified_issue: Approach: keep Seeed's Connector A/B quick-change instead of a new flange. Measured from 2-M6-ROTOR.step and 2-M7-STATOR.step with OCCT (cad/blender/.venv, cadquery-ocp + trimesh, gitignored). In link6 the J6 boss top is z 0, A spans 0–6, B −0.5–9, and motor 7's back face is at 9. Base 9's motor axis is Y (across the fingers), so a coaxial mount like the stock one would point the fingers sideways. Hence the L bracket on the RS00's back face (4 M3 Ø38 PCD 45°), with the J6 axis through (0, mount_axis_y=0) along Z. Rejected: mounting the base plate itself (its plane is XZ, normal Y, so its pillars can't take a Z-axis flange), and bracket+tool plate as one print (it would need a bore ceiling or leg overhang). The Aero pad pattern was measured from third_party/aero_hand/guide/anim41/left_base_link.STL; check_geometry recomputes it. Arm: vendored decimated meshes (20%; meshes_preview 5%); arm_pose.py is numpy-only FK. The arm check uses lod=full points against exports/assembly.stl, with 0.3 mm tolerance for the J6 boss inside the socket (decimation raises it ~0.26 mm; Seeed's original tops out at z 0.000). The *.stl gitignore is overridden only in cad/arm/rebot_b601_rs/.gitignore. Version exports stay untracked like Base 9's (run export_models.py on a fresh clone). Pre-existing failure, not mine: Scripts/test_gripper_poses.py fails for v306 (no poses.js entry). Unverified: stiffness, self-tap pull-out, connector clocking, real arm fit.
results.summary: Base 10: our gripper and the Aero Hand both mount on the reBot B601-RS wrist through Seeed's own interface. A hub stays on J6, each tool carries a tool plate and swaps with 3 radial screws. The arm CAD is in the repo and shows in the live preview.
results.detailed_description:
How the stock gripper mounts (measured from Seeed's STEP files): J6 is an RS00, the same motor as ours. Seeed's aluminium Connector A bolts to J6's output. Connector B bolts to the stock gripper motor's back face (4 M3 on a 38 mm circle), slips over A, and 3 radial M3 lock it. I kept that interface instead of inventing a new flange.

What Base 10 adds (v310_generalist_arm_mount, Base 9's gripper unchanged):
- Hub: a printed twin of Connector A. It stays on the arm, bolted to J6's 6 output holes. Seeed's aluminium one fits too.
- Tool plate: a printed twin of Connector B. Every tool carries one. Loosen 3 radial screws, lift the tool off, slide the other on.
- Wrist bracket (gripper only): our motor's axis runs across the fingers, so it can't sit on J6's axis like the stock motor. The bracket is an L. The leg bolts to the RS00's back face (the same 4 M3 that Connector B uses). The foot lies across the J6 axis, and the tool plate screws to it. The fingers point straight out along the wrist's roll axis, centred like the stock fingers.
- Aero Hand plate: the left Aero Hand's wrist pad has 4 M3 inserts on a 26.9 mm square, the same 38 mm circle at 45° (from its CAD). So its plate is the same tool plate plus an 8 mm spacer with a channel that carries the hand's USB and 6 V leads out sideways. That gives one hub on the arm and either tool on it.
- RS00 cabling: the two motor connectors are now on the motor model and checked clear of the bracket. The cable zip-ties through two slots in the foot and drops to J6, as the stock gripper's does.
- Everything prints without supports (teardrop holes, socket opening upward); the overhang check passes on all 11 printed parts.
- Arm CAD: Seeed's B601-RS URDF and meshes are in cad/arm/rebot_b601_rs/, pinned to their commit 9e8634c, licence CERN-OHL-W-2.0 (copied). arm_pose.py poses the arm for any tool. Base 10's preview shows the arm holding the gripper, with the Aero Hand on its plate beside it.

Screws: 6× M3×6 (hub to J6), 4× M3×8 (leg to motor), 4× M3×10 (tool plate to bracket), 3× M3×8 (radial), 4× M3×14 (Aero).

All 71 geometry checks pass, including: the arm stays clear of the gripper and mount (positive control: raised 3 mm, it hits), and the Aero inserts land on the tool-screw circle (0.0 mm off). Every new parameter is a params.json entry on the Tune panel.

Things to know: (1) The gripper now hangs by its motor's back face and sits ~70 mm out from the leg to the roll axis. I made the foot 8 mm thick but haven't checked stiffness at full payload. mount_axis_y −30 halves that reach, but then the fingers orbit 30 mm off the roll axis. (2) The radial and tool screws self-tap into print. Seeed's aluminium Connector A/B are the stronger choice if you have them. (3) Which way the motor's connectors point on your motor is assumed (motor_conn_deg). (4) The arm meshes are decimated (1–3 mm off), and nothing was printed or test-fitted on the real arm.
results.user_reply_draft: Hey Jake! The gripper now goes on the reBot arm the same way Seeed's own gripper does: a small hub stays on the wrist, and each tool has a plate that slips over it and locks with 3 screws. Our gripper and the Aero Hand each get one, so swapping them takes about a minute with a hex key. The arm itself now shows in the live preview holding the gripper. Everything prints without supports. One thing to try first: the gripper sits a little out from the wrist so its fingers stay centred, so give it a wiggle under load after printing and tell me if it flexes.

summary: Design a parameterized, support-free printable mount that bolts the gripper's next Base onto the Seeed reBot B601-RS wrist flange, with RS00 cabling routed. Also import the arm CAD into the live preview, and make one common flange adapter with swappable tool interfaces for the gripper and left Aero Hand.
